title: Cortés's march to Tenochtitlan
summary: In August 1519 Hernán Cortés led his Spanish force inland from Cempoala, fought and then allied with the Tlaxcalans, whose city he entered on 23 September, and sacked Cholula on 18 October. On 8 November 1519 the column reached the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, where Moctezuma II received it peacefully.

uncertainty.note: The Pressbooks timeline gives 16 Aug 1519 (leaving Cempoala), 23 Sep (entering Tlaxcala), 18 Oct (Cholula massacre) and 8 Nov 1519. The University of Kansas exhibit dates the first landing to Good Friday / April 1519 and the first meeting with Moctezuma to 8 November 1519. A History Hit article dates the arrival at the gates to 8 November 1519 and the departure from Cuba to February 1519. Death tolls at Cholula differ between pages and are not given here.

importance.justification: The inland march that brought Cortés's expedition and its Tlaxcalan allies to the Aztec capital, the start of the Spanish conquest of the Aztec empire.

audience_note: Describes the sack of Cholula, in which a large number of its people were killed in the courtyard of the Temple of Quetzalcoatl.

related.because: The march placed the Spanish and their allies in the Aztec capital, which they besieged and took in 1521.

beats.caption: Cortés leaves Cempoala for the highlands; after battles at Tlaxcala the army enters the city on 23 September and stays about three weeks.
At Cholula the Spaniards, who feared a plot, kill many people in the courtyard of the Temple of Quetzalcoatl.
On 8 November the column reaches Tenochtitlan, where Moctezuma receives it peacefully, placing the Spanish inside the Aztec capital.

reviewer_note: Least sure: day-level dates come from one online book chapter (class other) that cites Bernal Díaz and others; the University of Kansas exhibit and History Hit confirm 8 November 1519. Cholula is plotted at the Great Pyramid, not the town centre; the death toll is disputed across pages and omitted. Malinche is named in the chapter as learning of the Cholula plot; the link to her record is a general relation.
